questions.qtext: Which of the following represents the correct definition of a sample space in probability theory?

options.text: The collection of all possible outcomes of an experiment.
The likelihood of an event occurring.
The set of outcomes that have equal probability of occurring.
The event that consists of no outcomes.

questions.solution:
(a)
The sample space is defined as the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment or random process.

questions.qtext: If events A and B are independent, what is the probability of both events occurring?
questions.solution:
(a)
If events A and B are independent, the probability of both events occurring is the product of their individual probabilities, P(A) × P(B).
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements best describes the property of independent events?

options.text: The occurrence of one event affects the occurrence of the other event.
The occurrence of one event guarantees the occurrence of the other event.
The occurrence of one event does not affect the occurrence of the other event.
The occurrence of one event makes the occurrence of the other event impossible.

questions.solution:
(c)
Independent events are events where the occurrence of one event does not affect the occurrence of the other event.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: If events A and B are mutually exclusive, what is not the probability of either event A or event B occurring?
questions.solution:
(a, c, d)
If events A and B are mutually exclusive, the probability of either event A or event B occurring is the sum of their individual probabilities, P(A) + P(B).

questions.qtext: Which of the following best describes conditional probability?

options.text: The probability of two independent events occurring simultaneously.
The probability of an event occurring given that another event has already occurred.
The probability of two events occurring simultaneously without any dependency.
The probability of an event occurring without considering any other events.

questions.solution:
(b)
Conditional probability is the probability of an event A occurring given that another event B has already occurred. It represents the likelihood of event A happening under the condition that event B is known to have occurred. Therefore, option B is the correct definition of conditional probability.

questions.qtext:
How many statements are correct with respect to mutually exclusive events?
(A) Events that have no outcomes in common and can occur simultaneously.
(B) Events that have no outcomes in common and cannot occur simultaneously.
(C) Events that have some outcomes in common and can occur simultaneously.
(D) Events that have some outcomes in common and cannot occur simultaneously.

NAT
questions.solution:
1
(B) Events that have no outcomes in common and cannot occur simultaneously (correct). Mutually exclusive events refer to events where the occurrence of one event excludes the occurrence of the other event. In other words, if one event happens, the other event cannot happen at the same time. This means that mutually exclusive events have no outcomes in common and cannot occur simultaneously.
